q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of rusk per kg?
title: Rusk carbon footprint per kg
short: Rusk is bread baked twice: add flour, sugar and fat with supplier figures, then the oven fuel for both bakes, slicing and packing. Divide the bakery's energy by kg of rusk packed, which is less than the dough weight after drying.

ul: Wheat flour, sugar, fat and milk solids by weight.
Slicing and second bake to dry the slices.

p: Report per kg packed. Two bakes usually make rusk more energy intensive per kg than bread from the same oven.

example.title: Worked example: rusk unit per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 28,530 / 120,000 = 0.238 kg CO2 per kg
Add flour, sugar, fat and packing for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
